textbookText: v. Friedel- Craft’s reactions The reaction involves introduction of an alkyl group or an acyl group in the benzene ring in presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride as a Lewis acid. The reaction was proposed by Charles Friedel and Jame Mason Craft in 1877. The reactions are studied in two different types.
a. Friedel-Craft’s alkylation b. When benzene is heated with alkyl halide in presence

of anhydrous AlCl3, BF3, FeCl3, etc. alkyl group(-R) is added to the benzene ring. So, alkyl benzene is obtained. If methyl halide is used, methyl benzene is obtained, as well as if ethyl halide is used ethyl benzene is obtained and so on. Some examples are as follows.

c. Friedel-Craft’s acylation When benzene is heated with ac yl halide in presence of anhydrous AlCl3 and ether acyl group(RCO-) is added to the benzene ring. So, acyl benzene is obtained. If acetyl halide is used, acetophenone is obtained, as well as if acetic anyhydride is used acetophenone is obtained as a major product and so on. Some examples are as follows.

vi. Combustion of Benzene (free combustion) When benzene is combusted in the presence of air, it burns with a yellow luminous sooty flame and is oxidized into carbondi-oxide and water. 2C6H6 + 15O2 𝐶𝑜𝑚𝑏𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 → 12CO2 +6H2O Uses of Benzene

a. Used as organic solvent. b. Used as solvent for the extraction of fats and oils. c. Used as fuel in the name of benzol d. Starting material in the synthesis of dyes, drugs, plastics, perfumes, etc. e. Used in dry cleaning agents. f. Component of anti-knocking gaseline.
